subject: general
question: A solid metal hemisphere has a radius of 6 cm. If the metal of the hemisphere is melted and recast into a cylindrical shape with the same radius, find the height of the cylinder.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **solid hemisphere** is melted into a **cylinder** of the same radius, equate their volumes.

Volume of Hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r³

Volume of Cylinder = π × r² × h

Since radii are equal: (2/3) × r = h

h = (2/3) × 6 = 4 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius of Hemisphere (r)** = 6 cm

**Radius of Cylinder (R)** = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a **Hemisphere** = (2/3)πr³

Volume of a **Cylinder** = πR²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/983b4390cef9603404d996bf1f1b88edafd070850c1ca217a53b3cfff0df26cc.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of **Cylinder** = Volume of **Hemisphere**

⇒ π × (6)² × h = (2/3) × π × (6)³

⇒ 36 × h = (2/3) × 216

⇒ 36 × h = 2 × 72

⇒ 36 × h = 144

⇒ h = 144 ÷ 36

⇒ h = 4 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Conversion of Solids

When one solid object is melted to form another, the **Total Volume** remains constant, provided there is no wastage of material.

Properties of a Sphere

Volume of Sphere = (4/3)πr³ and Total Surface Area = 4πr². A hemisphere is exactly half of a sphere.

Cylinder Surface Area

Curved Surface Area = 2πrh and Total Surface Area = 2πr(h + r).</p
